chapter: Pianists, Basie, Lil Armstrong and closing
title: Lil in Paris, her compositions and uncredited writing
summary: She lived in France and taught French, and wrote tunes like Struttin' with Some Barbecue credited to Louis; Saunders loved her Clip Joint.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, she lived in the house that they had on --

All her life, right. I used to love to go down and hear her playing, and then she'd sing a lot of -- she went to France and she stayed over there -- oh, I don't know, for years, and she fell in love with Paris.
And then she learned to speak French fluently. And then she would come down and --
Oh, yeah. And then when she was -- just before she passed, she was teaching French at classes. She was teaching.

Yeah, and then she'd play those songs, 'Pardon, Pardon,' and she'd play all of these songs from France, and then she played a lot of her original things. She never did get credit for 'Strutting with Barbecue' and --
Well, they just had L. Armstrong, but it was Lil.

Lil Armstrong. See, she used to write -- see, Louis at that particular time was just more or less an ear type musician. She taught him how to read and things like that. She taught him a lot of things. And -- but she was the one that was really writing the tunes, and then when they would go into the studios, well, they would change the names on them. You know how the record business has always been shady like that.

So she would do it, and her 'Strutting with Some Barbecue,' and so many things that she wrote. And then this other thing, she used to do a tune called 'Clip Joint,' and I used to love to hear her -- every time, I'd say, 'Lil, sing Clip Joint for me.' That was one of my favorites.
